review_note: Reviewed 2026-10-24 from all eight native CASCI(19,14) product-side probes at 2, 3.5, 6 and 30 angstrom in aDZ-F12 and aTZ-F12. Select CAS(7,6) from noncontiguous 2 angstrom source indices 15,19,20,21,22,25. H2 sigma/sigma-star (15/25; occupations about 1.976/0.024) contribute two electrons, HCS2 pi/pi-star (19/22; about 1.917/0.139) contribute two, and its two sulfur-rich frontier combinations (20/21; about 1.542/1.450) contribute three. Retaining the H2 pair permits its bond relaxation to respond within the active space; this is a conservative chemical inclusion, not a measured compact-space energy-convergence result. Other C-S sigma pairs and deeper lone pairs remain inactive. Two equal-weight doublets are orbital support; only D1 is counted as reactive flux. The [6,4] coordinate separates HCS2 atoms [1,2,3,6] from H2 atoms [4,5] in the saved L2 exit complex; it does not stretch the internal H2 bond. Use separate basis-specific records and direct CASPT2-F12 aDZ/aTZ CBS, power 3.7. Compact CASSCF/CASPT2, angular convergence and relaxed state/connectivity continuity are not yet validated; inspect the production scan under its unchanged review gates. The outer RotdPy dividing surfaces use fragment centers of mass; their distances are COM separations. The one-dimensional relaxed/frozen correction remains the mapped interfragment anchor scan from the saved product complex. Both grids retain the explicit production distance lists; they are distinct coordinates and must not be interchanged.

states.energy_reference_note: One ground-parent adiabatic doublet path D1 relative to its spin-free ground-fragment asymptote. Other state-averaged roots support orbitals; they are not extra reactive flux.
